cases.region: In a multi-hop QA pipeline the first-hop summary is the only channel that carries retrieved evidence forward: the follow-up query stage, the second summary, and the final answer are produced without access to the original passages. Multi-hop questions are typically answered through a chain in which one passage names an intermediate entity and a later passage describes that entity; the intermediate entity, together with the relation connecting it to the question, is the bridge that makes the next retrieval possible. A retrieved passage can therefore carry two distinct kinds of value — direct answer facts, and bridge signals such as key entities, their relations, and any explicit pointer toward a still-missing document. When the next-hop document is already in the retrieved set, its entity and relation are themselves part of that bridge evidence; when it is absent, the bridge signal preserved in the summary is the only basis from which a follow-up query can be formed. A common failure mode is to fill an absent next-hop fact with plausible but unretrieved background knowledge (for example, a familiar attribute of a named entity): this replaces the missing bridge with an unsupported claim and removes the cue the retrieval stage would otherwise use to surface the correct document. This background illustrates why synthesizing across retrieved passages, rather than compressing only toward the direct answer, keeps the clues on which the later stages depend.
